source: The Song Celestial (Bhagavad-Gita), tr. Sir Edwin Arnold, 1885 (public domain; Project Gutenberg #2388), plus Bhagavad Gita verses: Sanskrit text (public domain) with English meanings written for DailyDivine.

verses.translatedText:
Find full reward
Of doing right in right! Let right deeds be
Thy motive, not the fruit which comes from them.
And live in action! Labour! Make thine acts
Thy piety, casting all self aside,
Contemning gain and merit; equable
In good or evil: equability
Is Yog, is piety!

If one
Ponders on objects of the sense, there springs
Attraction; from attraction grows desire,
Desire flames to fierce passion, passion breeds
Recklessness; then the memory--all betrayed--
Lets noble purpose go, and saps the mind,
Till purpose, mind, and man are all undone.

And whoso thus
Discerneth Me in all, and all in Me,
I never let him go; nor looseneth he
Hold upon Me; but, dwell he where he may,
Whate'er his life, in Me he dwells and lives,
Because he knows and worships Me, Who dwell
In all which lives, and cleaves to Me in all.

Nay, but as when one layeth
His worn-out robes away,
And taking new ones, sayeth,
"These will I wear to-day!"
So putteth by the spirit
Lightly its garb of flesh,
And passeth to inherit
A residence afresh.

Yet, the right act
Is less, far less, than the right-thinking mind.
Seek refuge in thy soul; have there thy heaven!

But, if one deals with objects of the sense
Not loving and not hating, making them
Serve his free soul, which rests serenely lord,
Lo! such a man comes to tranquillity;
And out of that tranquillity shall rise
The end and healing of his earthly pains,
Since the will governed sets the soul at peace.

Whoso shall offer Me in faith and love
A leaf, a flower, a fruit, water poured forth,
That offering I accept, lovingly made
With pious will. Whate'er thou doest, Prince!
Eating or sacrificing, giving gifts,
Praying or fasting, let it all be done
For Me, as Mine.

I say to thee weapons reach not the Life;
Flame burns it not, waters cannot o'erwhelm,
Nor dry winds wither it. Impenetrable,
Unentered, unassailed, unharmed, untouched,
Immortal, all-arriving, stable, sure,
Invisible, ineffable, by word
And thought uncompassed, ever all itself,
Thus is the Soul declared!

In sorrows not dejected, and in joys
Not overjoyed; dwelling outside the stress
Of passion, fear, and anger; fixed in calms
Of lofty contemplation;--such an one
Is Muni, is the Sage, the true Recluse!

I am alike for all! I know not hate,
I know not favour! What is made is Mine!
But them that worship Me with love, I love;
They are in Me, and I in them!

Nor I, nor thou, nor any one of these,
Ever was not, nor ever will not be,
For ever and for ever afterwards.
All, that doth live, lives always!

Finally, this is better, that one do
His own task as he may, even though he fail,
Than take tasks not his own, though they seem good.
To die performing duty is no ill;
But who seeks other roads shall wander still.

And like the ocean, day by day receiving
Floods from all lands, which never overflows
Its boundary-line not leaping, and not leaving,
Fed by the rivers, but unswelled by those;--

So is the perfect one! to his soul's ocean
The world of sense pours streams of witchery;
They leave him as they find, without commotion,
Taking their tribute, but remaining sea.

If one of evil life turn in his thought
Straightly to Me, count him amidst the good;
He hath the high way chosen; he shall grow
Righteous ere long; he shall attain that peace
Which changes not.

Of many thousand mortals, one, perchance,
Striveth for Truth; and of those few that strive--
Nay, and rise high--one only--here and there--
Knoweth Me, as I am, the very Truth.

What the wise choose
The unwise people take; what best men do
The multitude will follow.

Yea, the world is strong,
But what discerns it stronger, and the mind
Strongest; and high o'er all the ruling Soul.

Thou Prince of India!
Be certain none can perish, trusting Me!

I am the Spirit seated deep in every creature's heart;
From Me they come; by Me they live; at My word they depart!

Yea! let each play his part
In all he finds to do, with unyoked soul.

The world is overcome--aye! even here!
By such as fix their faith on Unity.

Who hateth nought
Of all which lives, living himself benign,
Compassionate, from arrogance exempt,
Exempt from love of self, unchangeable
By good or ill; patient, contented, firm
In faith, mastering himself, true to his word,
Seeking Me, heart and soul; vowed unto Me,--
That man I love!

The Light of Lights He is, in the heart of the Dark
Shining eternally. Wisdom He is
And Wisdom's way, and Guide of all the wise,
Planted in every heart.

Better thine own work is, though done with fault,
Than doing others' work, ev'n excellently.

Be not over-glad
Attaining joy, and be not over-sad
Encountering grief, but, stayed on Brahma, still
Constant let each abide!

Who troubleth not his kind,
And is not troubled by them; clear of wrath,
Living too high for gladness, grief, or fear,
That man I love!

There is "true" Knowledge. Learn thou it is this:
To see one changeless Life in all the Lives,
And in the Separate, One Inseparable.

He that acts in thought of Brahm,
Detaching end from act, with act content,
The world of sense can no more stain his soul
Than waters mar th' enamelled lotus-leaf.

Let each man raise
The Self by Soul, not trample down his Self,
Since Soul that is Self's friend may grow Self's foe.

Near to renunciation--very near--
Dwelleth Eternal Peace!

When Righteousness
Declines, O Bharata! when Wickedness
Is strong, I rise, from age to age, and take
Visible shape, and move a man with men,
Succouring the good, thrusting the evil back,
And setting Virtue on her seat again.

The sacrifice
Which Knowledge pays is better than great gifts
Offered by wealth, since gifts' worth--O my Prince!
Lies in the mind which gives, the will that serves:
And these are gained by reverence, by strong search,
By humble heed of those who see the Truth
And teach it.

Humbleness, truthfulness, and harmlessness,
Patience and honour, reverence for the wise.

There is no purifier like thereto
In all this world, and he who seeketh it
Shall find it--being grown perfect--in himself.

The gift lovingly given, when one shall say
"Now must I gladly give!" when he who takes
Can render nothing back; made in due place,
Due time, and to a meet recipient,
Is gift of Sattwan, fair and profitable.

But for earthly needs
Religion is not his who too much fasts
Or too much feasts, nor his who sleeps away
An idle mind; nor his who wears to waste
His strength in vigils. Nay, Arjuna! call
That the true piety which most removes
Earth-aches and ills, where one is moderate
In eating and in resting, and in sport;
Measured in wish and act; sleeping betimes,
Waking betimes for duty.

Fearlessness, singleness of soul, the will
Always to strive for wisdom; opened hand
And governed appetites; and piety,
And love of lonely study; humbleness,
Uprightness, heed to injure nought which lives,
Truthfulness, slowness unto wrath, a mind
That lightly letteth go what others prize;

Moreover, Son of Pandu! wert thou worst
Of all wrong-doers, this fair ship of Truth
Should bear thee safe and dry across the sea
Of thy transgressions.

Hero long-armed! beyond denial, hard
Man's heart is to restrain, and wavering;
Yet may it grow restrained by habit, Prince!
By wont of self-command.

The Doors of Hell
Are threefold, whereby men to ruin pass,--
The door of Lust, the door of Wrath, the door
Of Avarice. Let a man shun those three!

He is not lost, thou Son of Pritha! No!
Nor earth, nor heaven is forfeit, even for him,
Because no heart that holds one right desire
Treadeth the road of loss!

Words causing no man woe, words ever true,
Gentle and pleasing words, and those ye say
In murmured reading of a Sacred Writ,--
These make the true religiousness of Speech.

Serenity of soul, benignity,
Sway of the silent Spirit, constant stress
To sanctify the Nature,--these things make
Good rite, and true religiousness of Mind.

verses.originalText:
नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना ।
न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम् ॥
verses.translatedText: One who is not self-controlled has no steady wisdom and no meditation; without meditation there is no peace; and without peace, how can there be happiness?

verses.originalText:
समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः ।
ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम् ॥
verses.translatedText: I am the same to all beings; none is hateful to me, none is dear. But those who worship me with devotion are in me, and I am in them.

verses.originalText:
कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः ।
स बुद्धिमान् मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत् ॥
verses.translatedText: One who sees inaction in action and action in inaction is wise among people, is a yogi, and has accomplished all that is to be done.

verses.originalText:
यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति ।
तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति ॥
verses.translatedText: One who sees me everywhere and sees everything in me: I am never lost to that person, nor are they lost to me.

verses.originalText:
ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते ।
सङ्गात् संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥
verses.translatedText: Dwelling on the objects of the senses, a person grows attached to them; from attachment springs desire, and from desire anger arises.

verses.originalText:
मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु ।
मामेवैष्यसि युक्त्वैवमात्मानं मत्परायणः ॥
verses.translatedText: Fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, worship me, bow to me; thus united with me and intent on me, you will come to me.

verses.originalText:
यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः ।
स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ॥
verses.translatedText: Whatever a great person does, others follow; whatever standard they set, the world goes by.

verses.originalText:
मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः ।
आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ॥
verses.translatedText: O son of Kunti, the contact of the senses with their objects brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go and do not last: bear them patiently, O Bharata.

verses.originalText:
उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् ।
आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
verses.translatedText: Let a person lift themselves by their own self and not degrade themselves; for the self alone is one's friend, and the self alone is one's enemy.

verses.originalText:
सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज ।
अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ॥
verses.translatedText: Abandoning all duties, come to me alone for refuge. I will free you from all sins; do not grieve.

verses.originalText:
युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु ।
युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा ॥
verses.translatedText: For one who is moderate in food and recreation, moderate in effort at work, and moderate in sleep and waking, yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrow.

verses.originalText:
विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः ।
निर्ममो निरहंकारः स शांतिमधिगच्छति ॥
verses.translatedText: One who gives up all desires and moves through life free from longing, possessiveness and ego attains peace.

verses.originalText:
यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत ।
अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदाऽऽत्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ॥
verses.translatedText: Whenever righteousness declines and unrighteousness rises, O Bharata, I bring myself forth.

verses.originalText:
सर्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्टो मत्तः स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनं च ।
वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यो वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम् ॥
verses.translatedText: I dwell in the heart of all; from me come memory, knowledge and their loss. I alone am to be known through all the Vedas; I am the author of Vedanta and the knower of the Vedas.

verses.originalText:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन ।
मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
verses.translatedText: You have a right to your actions, but never to their fruits. Do not let the fruit of action be your motive, and do not cling to inaction.

verses.originalText:
असंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलं ।
अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥
verses.translatedText: The Lord said: Without doubt, O mighty-armed, the mind is restless and hard to restrain; but by practice and detachment, O son of Kunti, it can be held.

verses.originalText:
तेषां सततयुक्तानां भजतां प्रीतिपूर्वकम् ।
ददामि बुद्धियोगं तं येन मामुपयान्ति ते ॥
verses.translatedText: To those who are constantly devoted and worship me with love, I give the yoga of understanding by which they come to me.

verses.originalText:
योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय ।
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥
verses.translatedText: Established in yoga, do your work, O Dhananjaya, letting go of attachment and staying the same in success and failure. This evenness of mind is called yoga.

verses.originalText:
समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम् ।
विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥
verses.translatedText: One who sees the Supreme Lord dwelling equally in all beings, imperishable amid the perishing, truly sees.

verses.originalText:
यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः ।
हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ॥
verses.translatedText: One who does not disturb the world, and is not disturbed by the world, who is free from elation, impatience, fear and agitation, is dear to me.

verses.originalText:
सन्तुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः ।
मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥
verses.translatedText: The yogi who is always content, self-controlled, firm in resolve, with mind and intellect offered to me: such a devotee of mine is dear to me.

verses.originalText:
नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः ।
न चातिस्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन ॥
verses.translatedText: Yoga is not for one who eats too much or fasts completely, nor for one who sleeps too much or stays awake too much, O Arjuna.

verses.originalText:
त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः ।
कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ॥
verses.translatedText: Desire, anger and greed: these three are the gates of hell, destroying the self; therefore one should give up all three.

verses.originalText:
परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् ।
धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय संभवामि युगे युगे ॥
verses.translatedText: To protect the good, to destroy evildoers and to establish dharma, I come into being age after age.

verses.originalText:
देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा ।
तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ॥
verses.translatedText: Just as the embodied self passes through childhood, youth and old age in this body, so it passes into another body. The steady-minded are not troubled by this.

verses.originalText:
इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया ।
विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥
verses.translatedText: Thus I have told you knowledge more secret than any secret; reflect on it fully, then do as you wish.

verses.originalText:
पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति ।
तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः ॥
verses.translatedText: Whoever offers me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, that loving offering of a pure-hearted person I accept.

verses.originalText:
यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ।
स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः ॥
verses.translatedText: By worshipping, through one's own work, that from which all beings arise and by which all this is pervaded, a person attains perfection.

verses.originalText:
विद्याविनयसंपन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि ।
शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः ॥
verses.translatedText: The wise see with an equal eye a learned and humble brahmin, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and an outcaste (shvapaka).

verses.originalText:
ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम् ।
मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ॥
verses.translatedText: In whatever way people approach me, in that same way I receive them; people follow my path in every way, O Partha.

verses.originalText:
न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः ।
अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ॥
verses.translatedText: The self is never born and never dies, nor, having come to be, will it cease to be. Unborn, eternal, everlasting and ancient, it is not killed when the body is killed.

verses.originalText:
अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् ।
स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥
verses.translatedText: Speech that causes no distress, that is truthful, pleasing and beneficial, together with the regular study of scripture: this is called the discipline of speech.

verses.originalText:
समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः ।
शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्जितः ॥
verses.translatedText: The one who is the same toward foe and friend, in honour and dishonour, in cold and heat, in pleasure and pain, and free from attachment...

verses.originalText:
मच्चित्तः सर्वदुर्गाणि मत्प्रसादात्तरिष्यसि ।
अथ चेत्त्वमहङ्कारान्न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि ॥
verses.translatedText: With your mind on me, by my grace you will cross all obstacles; but if from ego you will not listen, you will be lost.

verses.originalText:
प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः ।
अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्ताऽहमिति मन्यते ॥
verses.translatedText: All actions are carried out by the qualities of nature; but one deluded by ego thinks, 'I am the doer.'

verses.originalText:
न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते ।
तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति ॥
verses.translatedText: Truly, nothing in this world purifies like knowledge. One perfected in yoga finds it within the self in due time.

verses.originalText:
क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः संमोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः ।
स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ॥
verses.translatedText: From anger comes delusion; from delusion, confusion of memory; from confusion of memory, the loss of discernment; and from the loss of discernment, a person is ruined.

verses.originalText:
अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते ।
तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ॥
verses.translatedText: To those who worship me with undivided devotion, thinking of me alone, ever steadfast, I bring what they lack and preserve what they have.

verses.originalText:
नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते ।
स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
verses.translatedText: On this path no effort is lost and no harm results. Even a little of this practice protects from great fear.

verses.originalText:
दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः ।
वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते ॥
verses.translatedText: One whose mind is not shaken by sorrows, who does not crave pleasures, and who is free from attachment, fear and anger is called a sage of steady wisdom.

verses.originalText:
अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च ।
निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी ॥
verses.translatedText: One who hates no being, who is friendly and compassionate, free from possessiveness and ego, the same in pain and pleasure, and forgiving...

verses.originalText:
वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि ।
तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णान्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही ॥
verses.translatedText: As a person casts off worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, so the embodied self casts off worn-out bodies and enters new ones.

verses.originalText:
तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर ।
असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः ॥
verses.translatedText: Therefore, without attachment, always do the work that needs to be done; for a person who works without attachment reaches the highest.

verses.originalText:
बन्धुरात्माऽऽत्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः ।
अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ॥
verses.translatedText: For one who has conquered the self by the self, the self is a friend; but for one who has not, the self behaves like an enemy.

verses.originalText:
यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः ।
तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम ॥
verses.translatedText: Where Krishna, lord of yoga, is, and where Arjuna the archer is, there are prosperity, victory, well-being and steady justice: this is my conviction.

verses.originalText:
दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया ।
मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते ॥
verses.translatedText: This divine power of mine, made of the three qualities, is hard to cross; but those who take refuge in me alone cross beyond it.

verses.originalText:
सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ ।
ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥
verses.translatedText: Treating pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat alike, then engage in the battle; in this way you will incur no sin.

verses.originalText:
आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत् ।
तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी ॥
verses.translatedText: As waters flow into the sea, ever full and unmoved, so the one in whom all desires flow without disturbing him attains peace; not the one who runs after desires.

verses.originalText:
तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु मामनुस्मर युध्य च ।
मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्मामेवैष्यस्यसंशयम् ॥
verses.translatedText: Therefore remember me at all times and fight; with mind and intellect offered to me, you will surely come to me alone.
